newsitem.title: USA: Ralston may become top U.S. general - officials.
newsitem.headline: Ralston may become top U.S. general - officials.

text.p: Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston has apparently emerged at or near the top of a short list of candidates to become chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff, defence officials said on Wednesday.,

The officials cautioned in response to questions that a Marine Corps general was also in the race and Defence Secretary William Cohen had not made a recommendation to President Bill Clinton on who should succeed Army Gen. John Shalikashvili, who retires on Sept. 30 as the nation's top military officer.

The officials, who asked not to be identified, confirmed a New York Times report on Wednesday that Ralston, 53-year-old deputy chairman of the joint chiefs, was at or near the top of the list and that Cohen's recommendation could come next week.

The other name mentioned prominently in reports has been Marine Corps Gen. John Sheehan, outspokem head of the United States Atlantic Command based in Norfolk, Virginia. Sheehan, 56, who played a prominent role in U.S. military intervention in Haiti three years ago, has made enemies in the top ranks for his blunt remarks about the military and its bureaucracy.
"I would say it is now between Ralston and Sheehan," said one official of the two decorated Vietnam War veterans. "My bet is on Ralston."

"He (Ralston) is very smart, very smooth" said another official, stressing that the Air Force general had impressed Cohen with his work in a recent new analysis of U.S. military strategy and forces known as the Quadrennial Defence Review.
The Times reported that Shalikashvili had recommended Ralston to succeed him.
The officials said Cohen was expected to meet with Clinton as early as next week so the nomination could be made in time for the Senate to vote before the August congressional recess.
